title: Console compact telemetry cutset and phased MVP
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: This ticket documents a deliberately reduced MVP scope for Console observability surface: dashboards, tracing, and route-level cost breakdown. We must ship a useful but lightweight experience that demonstrates value to customers while avoiding high-cost aggregation pipelines and late integrations. This document captures what stays, what is cut, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and follow-up backlog items.
problem_statement: Original scope included comprehensive per-route cost breakdown, full-span distributed tracing with deep flamegraphs, and long retention dashboards. Those features require multiple infra changes, expensive aggregation jobs, and cross-team dependencies which threaten the March ship window and the budget for the MVP. We need a compacted scope that preserves core customer value: surface hotspots, basic trace sampling, and a cost signal sufficient for troubleshooting.
goals: Deliver a minimal yet actionable Console observability experience within the release window
Keep backend compute and query complexity low to meet cost targets
Provide graceful degradation paths and clear roadmap for re-adding cut features
Enable decision-making for Dedicated & Private customers with limited telemetry
non_goals: Full per-token/per-invocation cost accounting for every route
High-cardinality trace search or span-level flamegraph generation
Long-term raw telemetry retention (>30 days) in MVP
proposed_mvp_scope: Three dashboard cards: overall health (latency/errors), top 10 routes by 95th latency, aggregate cost rate (hourly) for top routes
Trace sampling at 1% globally with deterministic sampling on errors (up to 5% when error spike detected)
Route-level cost signal computed from sampled request rates + model-unit costs (approximation), not full token accounting
Simple card drilldown to recent traces (sampled) and direct link to route config
Basic alerting hooks for SLO breaches (email/pager) using existing alerting infra
trimmed_features_and_reasons: Per-token cost breakdown removed: requires token-level telemetry and large aggregation pipelines — defer to post-MVP optimization
Full distributed flamegraphs removed: expensive and low immediate ROI for early customers
Custom dashboard builder postponed: accelerates shipping by shipping predefined cards only
90-day retention removed: MVP will support 7-day retention to reduce storage costs
Immediate integration with customer KMS audit logs deferred to Private rollout due to security approvals
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Dashboard main view loads in <1.5s for typical accounts and shows three cards with current-data placeholders where necessary
AC2: Trace sampling pipeline returns sampled traces for a route within 2s of click-through from a card
AC3: Aggregate hourly cost signal for top routes is available and matches simulated cost estimates within +/-15%
AC4: Alerts can be created against the 95th latency metric and fire for synthetic breach during QA
AC5: Feature flags exist for toggling sampling rate and for enabling extended retention in Dedicated/Private deployments
rollout_plan: Phase A (internal beta): enable for Redwood internal orgs only, monitor costs and false positives — 1 week
Phase B (limited external beta): 3 pilot customers on hosted plan, collect feedback and telemetry — 2 weeks
Phase C (general availability light): enable for all hosted accounts with clear doc notes about limited retention and sampling — GA
Fallback: if cost exceeds threshold, reduce global sample rate to 0.25% and switch some cards to cached snapshots
monitoring_and_metrics: M1: Backend telemetry pipeline cost (USD/day) must be < target budget (TBD) for first 30 days
M2: Dashboard load p95 < 2s for 95% of requests
M3: Trace retrieval success rate >= 99% for sampled traces
M4: Customer satisfaction NPS question in pilot feedback >= 3/5 for observability usefulness
open_questions: Q1: Exact budget threshold for telemetry pipeline cost to keep — PM to confirm with finance
Q2: Should customer-facing docs expose sampling percentages per-route or keep opaque?
Q3: Do Dedicated customers require immediate parity (higher retention) or can we keep a separate upgrade path?
decisions: D1: Ship predefined card set rather than custom builder to reduce frontend scope
D2: Use sampling+approximation for cost signal rather than precise token accounting for MVP
D3: Default retention set to 7 days for hosted MVP, with upgrade path for Dedicated/Private
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers expect precise billing data — Mitigation: clearly label cost signal as approximate and add upgrade path doc
Risk: Sampling misses critical traces — Mitigation: deterministic sampling for error traces and on-demand increased sampling via feature flag
Risk: Aggregation jobs spike infra cost — Mitigation: limit top-route aggregation window and throttle background jobs during peak
follow_up_work: PM-611224: Reintroduce per-token cost breakdown design and estimate
ENG-2399: Long-retention pipeline and cold storage plan
notes: This compact MVP should be communicated clearly in release notes and in onboarding copy — highlight sampling and retention limits. Track pilot customer feedback closely to determine priority of reintroducing trimmed features.
